sources.entry: SkillSpector by NVIDIA - Security scanner for AI agent skills. Detect vulnerabilities, malicious patterns, and security risks.

summary.one_liner: SkillSpector is a security scanner that checks AI agent skills (for tools like Claude Code, Codex CLI, and Gemini CLI) for vulnerabilities, malicious patterns, and risky behavior before they are installed.
summary.what_it_does: Scans agent skills from Git repos, URLs, zip files, directories, or single files, using 71 vulnerability patterns across 17 categories such as prompt injection, data exfiltration, supply chain, taint tracking, AST-based dangerous code checks, YARA signatures, and MCP tool poisoning. It runs a fast static analysis stage and an optional LLM semantic stage, with a configurable OpenAI-compatible or hosted/local provider. It looks up known CVEs live via OSV.dev with an offline fallback. It produces a 0-100 risk score with severity labels and an install recommendation, and outputs terminal, JSON, Markdown, or SARIF reports. It supports baselines to suppress accepted findings so re-scans show only new issues, and can run as an MCP server so agents can call it as a tool to gate installs.
use_cases: check an agent skill for malicious code before installing it
gate Claude Code or other agent skill installs in CI
scan MCP server registry entries for security issues
audit third-party skills for prompt injection and data exfiltration
suppress known false positives and track only new findings
generate SARIF reports for code scanning pipelines
how_to_run: claude mcp add skillspector -- skillspector mcp
notable: Pattern catalog covers 71 checks across 17 categories, including AST, taint-flow, YARA, and MCP least-privilege and tool-poisoning rules
Two-stage analysis: static rules first, optional LLM semantic review
Baseline files with fingerprint or glob rules to suppress accepted findings and keep re-scans focused on new issues
Runs as an MCP server (stdio or loopback HTTP) so agents can call scan_skill before installing
Part of the NVIDIA Verified Skills pipeline that scans, evaluates, and signs skills
caveats: The HTTP MCP transport has no authentication and only binds to loopback addresses; remote access requires an external authenticating proxy
LLM analysis needs provider credentials or a local CLI setup; the README notes DeepSeek structured-output issues and that some providers and models have limits
Full install of the MCP server requires the optional mcp extra; the README notes an open issue with the stdio initialize hang
